architecture.mechanism: Multidirectional (360-degree) multichannel ultrasonic sensor array with strategic spatial positioning, empirically validated to maintain 97.5% detection accuracy under controlled rain (50 mm/h) and fog conditions, with robust performance at mid-to-long detection ranges despite reduced near-range performance in rain.
architecture.intervention: Replace or supplement the front AEB sensor suite on the 2020 Nissan Rogue with a multidirectional multichannel ultrasonic sensor array, strategically positioned across the front fascia to provide redundant spatial coverage that tolerates sensor contamination (mud, salt, ice, dust) because contamination-induced blockage of any single channel does not eliminate detection coverage; integrate with the existing AEB controller via sensor fusion so that ultrasonic confirmation corroborates radar/camera triggers and suppresses false-positive AEB activations caused by contamination on a single sensing modality.
architecture.expected_effect: Reliable automatic emergency braking activation in inclement weather (rain, fog) with suppression of false-positive activations triggered by front-sensor contamination, since the multichannel array maintains aggregate detection accuracy even when one or more channels are occluded by road grime or precipitation residue, while preserving true-positive emergency braking performance for actual forward collision threats.
architecture.falsification_test: On a contaminated-vehicle test track, deliberately coat the primary front sensor (camera/radar) with uniform mud splatter to reproduce the false-AEB condition, then run the multidirectional ultrasonic array through (a) a controlled rain chamber at 50 mm/h and (b) a fog chamber; record (1) false-positive AEB activations per 100 km of contaminated driving and (2) true-positive AEB activation latency against a standardized pedestrian surrogate at 45 mph. Pass criterion: false-positive rate drops by ≥80% versus the single-sensor baseline while true-positive detection latency remains within 150 ms of baseline at mid-to-long range.
